endorsements.title: Guardrails for GenAI drafted replies in patient portal messaging
endorsements.issuer: Sakr J. npj Digital Medicine 2026;9 (PMID 41942581, doi:10.1038/s41746-026-02621-6)
endorsements.quote: - Tier 3 (high risk): drafting disabled or mandatory second check (team member or structured checklist) + documentation of reasoning.

evidence.title: Radiologist Detection of Deficiencies in LLM-Generated Patient Communications About Radiology Reports: A Multi-Reader Study
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Miss rate of deficiencies with second reader review versus single reader
evidence.effect: Dual-reader review cut average miss rate from 12.4% (single) to 0.6%; triple-reader review detected all deficiencies.
evidence.quote: Dual-reader oversight significantly improves the safety and reliability of LLM-based communication tools.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated answers to simulated patient questions

commentary.bottom_line: One offline study of 1,200 LLM-generated answers to simulated patient questions found that adding a second reader cut the average miss rate for deficiencies from 12.4% to 0.6%. No study has tested a documented second check on real high-risk portal messages or measured its effect on patients.

perspectives.view: The only test is a single retrospective replay with raters, in simulated conditions, on 1,200 answers to invented patient questions. It measured detection of deficiencies rather than patient outcomes, and it did not limit analysis to high-risk message tiers. Indirectness and reliance on one study place certainty at very low, even though the effect favored dual review.

A single reader missed an average of 12.4% of deficiencies, and a second reader lowered that to 0.6%, with triple review detecting all of them. These figures suggest that one reviewer may let a meaningful share of errors through. The study did not grade miss severity, so the harm that the second check prevents remains unmeasured.

The study took place offline, so it did not capture time pressure, inbox volume, or how reviewers would record their reasoning in the portal. It also did not compare a second clinician with the structured checklist option that the endorsing guidance allows. Fidelity and burden of the check in live workflows have not been tested.

The study reported miss rates but no reviewer time, staffing, or cost data. Health systems therefore cannot estimate from this evidence what a second check would cost per high-risk message. The endorsing guidance lets systems disable drafting in the high-risk tier instead, which may cost less where message volume is high.

commentary.research_gap: Prospective studies should compare single review, second clinician review, and structured checklist review on real high-risk portal messages, and measure severity of missed errors, reviewer time, reply delay, and patient harm.
commentary.underserved_note: The single study used simulated patient questions and reported no information on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether second checks catch errors at the same rate in translated or plain-language replies to these patients is unknown.
